current.text: He has a torn labrum in his shoulder. Recovery usually takes about six months, so the expected return is mid to late March.
Do not draft him or stash him on IL.
If he returns in March, he could disrupt the Phoenix center rotation during the fantasy playoffs.
Experts expect him to lose the starting job and become a backup big. One projection puts him at 16 to 17 minutes a night.
With Williams out, Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach have both started at center in preseason and play similar minutes.
He re-signed with Phoenix for 3 years and 38 million USD, about 13 million USD a year.
One expert thinks Phoenix signed him mainly so it can trade him at the deadline or within a year.
Phoenix has 4 games in each of our playoff weeks 19 to 21 and the fewest back-to-backs in the league.

durable.text: He is a low-usage big man who lives around the rim. His value comes from a high FG%, good FT% and rebounds.
His FG% is a league outlier on solid volume, and he gives good FT% too, a rare mix for a big.
He makes no threes and is not a big shot blocker for a center.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.
He misses many games. Even with load management, minutes limits and skipped back-to-backs, he played only 60 games last season.

note: Leave him out of our draft. He is out until mid to late March with a torn labrum, ESPN values him at 0 USD (rank 313), and even Yahoo's 5 USD (rank 221) is too much in a 144-player auction. Our league paid 9 USD for him last season. Watch Phoenix news in March: if he comes back healthy, his FG% and rebounds could help a punt 3PM team in our playoffs, since Phoenix plays 4-4-4 in weeks 19 to 21. Expect a backup role behind Maluach or Ighodaro, though.
